section_summary: This section begins with several long August 1943 Dōmei press intercepts combining Axis war reports, Japanese and collaborationist economic news, and propaganda concerning Burma, India, China, the Philippines, French Indochina, and the Pacific. The later papers document State Department efforts to obtain more systematic coverage of Japanese domestic and imperial broadcasting, including establishment of experimental medium-wave monitoring in Hawaii. The final portion consists largely of Federal Communications Commission forwarding letters and repeated 1944 intercepts of Jakarta Radio's Morse-code announcement promoting its English-language “American Hour.”

subfiles.title: Dōmei press intercept: Asian, European, and Pacific news items
subfiles.from: Dōmei News Agency, stations JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Foreign broadcast listeners and monitoring services
subfiles.about: A lengthy Dōmei transmission reports political, economic, military, and propaganda stories from Japanese-occupied Asia and the war fronts.
subfiles.summary: The intercept begins in the middle of reports about Ba Maw's accommodation with Karen representatives and Japanese war artists working in Burma. Later items address Japanese swimming and electric-power programs, the Sicilian and Soviet fronts, Wang Jingwei's Shanghai visit, Subhas Chandra Bose's relations with Thailand and Burma, Philippine reconstruction, Indochinese rice and cotton controls, and Japanese naval claims in the Solomon Islands. Several items promote imminent Philippine independence and condemn the former American occupation.

subfiles.title: Dōmei intercept: American occupation, Shōnan song, and Bose statement
subfiles.from: Dōmei News Agency, station JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Foreign broadcast listeners and monitoring services
subfiles.about: The transmission combines anti-American Philippine propaganda with a story about a Japanese soldiers' song and Bose's account of Thai support.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: American rule in the Philippines contrasted with Japanese-sponsored independence, a Shōnan song, and Bose's talk with Phibunsongkhram saying Thailand supports the Indian Independence League and INA.

subfiles.title: Dōmei press broadcast of August 14, 1943
subfiles.from: Dōmei News Agency, stations JUP/JUQ
subfiles.to: Foreign broadcast listeners and monitoring services
subfiles.about: Dōmei reports on a Chinese agricultural delegation, Wang Jingwei's Shanghai activities, and an Indonesian-Malayan inspection party visiting Japan.
subfiles.summary: Domei of August 14, 1943: a Chinese agricultural youth corps returns from Japan and Manchuria; praise of Wang Jingwei for financiers' cooperation and attacks on Anglo-American influence; Sumatra and Malaya delegates praise Japanese leadership.

subfiles.title: Dōmei French-language intercept: Indochina, Shanghai, and Laurel
subfiles.from: Dōmei News Agency, stations JAP/JUP
subfiles.to: Foreign broadcast listeners and monitoring services
subfiles.about: A French-language Dōmei transmission covers Indochinese cotton policy, Ambassador Yoshizawa's move to Saigon, Wang Jingwei's Shanghai visit, and José Laurel's administrative work.
subfiles.summary: French Domei intercept: Indochina raises cotton prices for industry, Yoshizawa's move to Saigon signals southern importance, Wang Jingwei's Shanghai influence, and Laurel meeting governors and drafting the Philippine organic law.

subfiles.title: Dōmei intercept: China fighting and Aguinaldo on American occupation
subfiles.from: Dōmei News Agency, stations JAP/JUP
subfiles.to: Foreign broadcast listeners and monitoring services
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports Japanese operations in China, Shanghai cotton controls, and Emilio Aguinaldo's denunciation of the American seizure of Manila.
subfiles.summary: Domei intercept: Japanese communiqué claims victories near Weishan Lake and capture of Colonel Liu Han-kung, a Shanghai cotton purchase office, and Aguinaldo accusing Dewey and Americans of destroying the First Philippine Republic.

subfiles.title: Request for complete Radio Reports on the Far East
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Robert D. Leigh, Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service
subfiles.about: Ballantine requests a complete file and an additional copy of the Radio Reports on the Far East for eventual use by the reopened American Embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine says FBIS Radio Reports on the Far East will help the future Tokyo Embassy and asks three copies of future issues instead of two.
keywords: Radio Reports on the Far East

subfiles.title: Commendation for Chungking economic-broadcast compilation
subfiles.from: R. C. Miller, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.to: Raymond H. Geist, Department of State
subfiles.about: Miller commends the Chungking Embassy's indexed selection of economic reports from Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Miller says the Bureau found Chungking despatch 1115 of August 7, prepared under Carl Boehringer for OEW, exceptionally useful, and asks that the Embassy staff be commended.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: ratification of the new Philippine constitution
subfiles.from: State Department PI (Lockhart)
subfiles.to: State Department decimal files
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to a memorandum summarizing Japanese broadcasts on ratification of the new Philippine constitution.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: ratification of the new Philippine constitution; the original is in another State Department file (894.76/153).

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Seiichi Murata's Tokyo shortwave broadcasts
subfiles.from: Justice Department (Hoover)
subfiles.to: Department of State
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to correspondence requesting information about Seiichi Murata, reportedly broadcasting by shortwave from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Seiichi Murata's Tokyo shortwave broadcasts; original Justice Department correspondence filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: FCC forwarding letter and Jakarta Radio intercept
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards another intercept of Jakarta Radio's American-directed announcement.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed Morse intercept identifies station PMC on 18,135 kilocycles and announces Jakarta Radio's “American Hour.” It promises important news and international-affairs revelations intended for listeners in the United States and urges them to listen directly to Jakarta.

subfiles.title: Japanese Affairs approval of proposed FCC monitoring request
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese Affairs
subfiles.to: Francis C. de Wolf
subfiles.about: The division approves a proposed Secretary of State letter seeking additional Japanese-broadcast monitoring, subject to wording changes.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Affairs welcomes more information from and about Japan, asks that 'Far Eastern Department' read 'Division of Japanese Affairs', and suggests, without objecting to keeping, dropping the claim that broadcasts can be intercepted in Hawaii part of the year.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese Affairs review of monitoring letter
subfiles.from: Telecommunications Division
subfiles.to: H. Merrell Benninghoff
subfiles.about: The Telecommunications Division asks whether a modified FBIS draft on increased monitoring of Japanese broadcasts is acceptable.
subfiles.summary: Routing note sends a proposed FBIS letter to FCC Chairman James Fly for Japanese Affairs' approval.

subfiles.title: FBIS proposal and draft letter requesting medium-wave monitoring
subfiles.from: Robert L. Leigh, Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service
subfiles.to: Francis C. de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.about: Leigh submits a draft Secretary of State letter supporting expanded West Coast monitoring of Japanese medium-wave broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: The proposed letter argues that Japanese domestic and imperial broadcasts would illuminate popular psychological reactions and provide detailed political and economic information. It asks FCC Chairman Fly to expand interception, noting that reception may be possible from the Hawaiian Islands during part of the year.

subfiles.title: State Department request for expanded Japanese broadcast interception
subfiles.from: Adolf A. Berle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: The State Department formally asks the FCC to obtain greater coverage of Japanese domestic and imperial medium-wave broadcasting.
subfiles.summary: Berle says Japanese broadcasts reveal psychological reactions and political and economic intelligence; asks the FCC to intercept as many medium-wave broadcasts as possible and study Hawaiian reception.

subfiles.title: Guidance on Japanese broadcast material desired by the State Department
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Acheson identifies the political and economic subjects the Department wants extracted from Japanese domestic and imperial broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Department asks for material on cabinet meetings, legislation, production, finance, travel, public meetings and local conditions, and for analysts to note discrepancies between domestic and foreign-directed broadcasts.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs recommendations for FBIS monitoring
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: H. G. Kelly, Telecommunications Division
subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs specifies the kinds of Japanese broadcast material it wants FBIS to monitor.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs requests broad political and economic material, comparison of domestic and foreign presentations, and avoiding duplication of regular FBIS summaries.

subfiles.title: Request to Far Eastern Affairs for monitoring requirements
subfiles.from: Telecommunications Division
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: The Telecommunications Division asks Far Eastern Affairs what material it wants from monitored Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Note directs attention to the last paragraph of the FCC letter and seeks subject guidance for FBIS analysts.

subfiles.title: Foreign Activity Correlation routing note
subfiles.from: O. P. Varney, Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.to: DCR
subfiles.about: Varney asks that the attached paper be recorded and routed appropriately.
subfiles.summary: This is a short administrative instruction. It documents the internal circulation of the FCC correspondence concerning Japanese broadcast monitoring.

subfiles.title: FCC reply on expanded Japanese monitoring and Hawaiian experiment
subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Fly reports that the FCC is expanding Japanese broadcast coverage and establishing an experimental Hawaiian medium-wave interception unit.
subfiles.summary: FCC says expansion will follow translator and funding availability, an experimental Hawaiian unit will test medium-wave interception, and it asks the Department for priority guidance.

subfiles.title: FCC forwarding letter and Jakarta Radio intercept of July 2
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards an intercept of the Jakarta Radio announcement to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed hand-keyed transmission identifies PMC on 18,135 kilocycles and announces a one-hour program beginning at 6 p.m. Pacific War Time. It claims the station will provide important international news unavailable from American sources and urges listeners to follow Jakarta's American programs.

subfiles.title: Second FCC forwarding letter and Jakarta Radio intercept of July 2
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: A second forwarding packet contains another reception of Jakarta Radio's standard American-program announcement.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure repeats PMC's call to the United States, frequency, schedule, and promise of otherwise unavailable international news. It closes by advertising another broadcast at 11:30 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC forwarding letter with two Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling transmits two further copies of Jakarta Radio's recurring American Hour announcement.
subfiles.summary: Both intercepts identify station PMC near 18,135 kilocycles and solicit American listeners with promises of important news and revelations. Reception notes record weak signals, interference, and poor or sloppy hand keying. Each announcement promotes a subsequent program around 11:30 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with July 28 Jakarta Radio intercept
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards a July 28 Santa Ana intercept of Jakarta Radio's announcement to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The intercepted station gives call sign PMC, frequency 18,135 kilocycles, and an 18:00 Pacific War Time starting hour. It characterizes the forthcoming material as important international news unavailable elsewhere and advertises a later Tokyo-time broadcast.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with second July 28 Jakarta Radio intercept
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards another July 28 reception of Jakarta Radio's standard American-program warning flash.
subfiles.summary: The text again identifies PMC and promotes a one-hour program of news and international revelations for the United States. Monitoring notes describe poor, very sloppy hand keying but little radio interference.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with Jakarta Radio intercept of early August
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC supplies another intercept of Jakarta Radio's promotional call to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure repeats the station's 18,135-kilocycle frequency and 18:00 Pacific War Time schedule. The monitor notes that the hand-sent code began very slowly and accelerated near the end, which advertised the following broadcast for 11:30 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with three Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards three receptions of Jakarta Radio's almost identical American Hour announcement.
subfiles.summary: FCC letter with three Jakarta Radio intercepts: PMC on 18,135 kilocycles urges Americans to hear international news unavailable elsewhere; poor keying, fading and interference.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with additional Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The packet contains further complete and partial intercepts of Jakarta Radio's recurring American-directed sign-on.
subfiles.summary: The transmissions repeat PMC's frequency, Pacific War Time schedule, promise of international revelations, and invitation to hear the American programs. One enclosure is represented by two sheets whose text runs from the opening call through the closing announcement of the next Tokyo-time broadcast. Reception annotations emphasize hand-keyed transmission quality.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with two Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling sends two more monitored versions of Jakarta Radio's American Hour promotional message.
subfiles.summary: Both intercepts address the United States and state that PMC will transmit important news and revelations over wireless telephony. They give the usual frequency near 18,135 kilocycles and advertise the next broadcast at approximately 11:30 or 11:35 Tokyo time. Monitoring notes mention poor hand sending and moderate atmospheric noise.

subfiles.title: FCC letter with partial and complete Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards one partial and one fuller intercept of Jakarta Radio's call to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: The first enclosure preserves only the closing statement and next-broadcast time after a strong unmodulated carrier. The second records most of the standard PMC announcement but includes pauses, corrupt passages, and corrections. Reception notes contrast good hand sending on one sheet with disrupted or incomplete modulation.

subfiles.title: FCC forwarding letter and Jakarta Radio intercept of late August
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, FCC Radio Intelligence Division
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards another noisy, poorly keyed interception of Jakarta Radio's announcement to the United States.
subfiles.summary: FCC letter and late-August Jakarta Radio intercept: the standard promise of important news and appeal to listen to American programs, with heavy interference and poor keying.
